name: halong.jpg
title: File:Karst HaLongBay Vietnam (pixinn.net).jpg
usage: Hạ Long Bay: solid limestone, liquid sea and gaseous air in one frame, for the slide that introduces matter and the three states. Chosen over an iceberg or a geyser because it is the class's own country — 'everything here is matter' lands harder when 'here' is somewhere they have been.

name: hourglass.jpg
title: File:Hourglass with flowing sand.jpg
usage: Sand pouring in a clear stream through the neck of an hourglass — the deck's opening hook (is sand a liquid?) and, twelve slides later, half of the compare slide that answers it. Chosen over a sand dune because the falling STREAM is what makes the class say 'liquid', and a dune does not have one.

name: ice.jpg
title: File:Ice cubes openphoto.jpg
usage: A stack of ice cubes, every one of them still a cube, for the properties of a solid. Deliberately water rather than a brick or a rock: the same substance appears as a liquid two slides later, so 'solid' reads as a state rather than as a kind of stuff. It is also a tile in the Word Wall.

name: mercury.jpg
title: File:Pouring liquid mercury bionerd.jpg
usage: Liquid mercury being poured into a dish — a metal that splashes. Paired with the hourglass on the 'you cannot tell by looking' compare slide: sand pours and is a solid, mercury is a metal and is a liquid. Both are baited tiles in the Word Wall at the end of the deck.

name: balloon.jpg
title: File:Cappadocia Balloon Inflating Wikimedia Commons.JPG
usage: The inside of a hot-air balloon being inflated, with a person standing in it for scale. The Learner's Book photograph on p.32 is a balloon in flight, which shows a balloon; this one shows a GAS filling every corner of an enormous container, which is the property being taught.
